reading.body:
Korbank is a Polish IT services company, not a large data center, and its OpenStreetMap tag as a data center most likely reflects a corporate office running internal IT rather than commercial colocation.

The record carries no megawatt figure, no operator, and no website, and its own research note states the identification could not be independently re-confirmed. What remains is a name, a coordinate near Wrocław, and a plausible match to a known Polish software and infrastructure firm. The tag says data center, but nothing in the data supports scale.

For AI specifically, this matters as a boundary case. The binding constraints on AI scaling are power and large facilities, and a facility with zero recorded megawatts and an unconfirmed operator is not part of that story. Treating every data center tag as compute capacity would overstate the map.

The data does not tell the reader whether Korbank operates any hosting at all, how large it is, or whether the tag is accurate. It covers one point in Poland on one date, with the confirming research explicitly unfinished.
